text:
miguel: Heads-up — our Android sample app crashes on 5.1 when retries are enabled in the SDK. Repro: emulator API 22, enable RetryPolicy.EXPONENTIAL in SampleActivity.

sophia: stacktrace?

miguel: java.lang.NetworkOnMainThreadException
    at android.os.StrictMode$AndroidBlockGuardPolicy.onNetwork(StrictMode.java:...)
    at java.net.PlainSocketImpl.socketConnect(PlainSocketImpl.java:...)
    ...

miguel: Minimal repro: in the sample's Retrofit module we used `CoroutineCallAdapter()` instead of the safe enqueuing wrapper; the adapter can dispatch on the caller thread. If you combine that with our `RetryInterceptor` which performs synchronous `call.execute()` inside `intercept`, it can retrigger network on the main thread.

kevin: hmm can you paste interceptor ordering? iirc application interceptors run before authenticators so they may call `execute()` on whatever thread created the call.

miguel: snippet:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .addInterceptor(RetryInterceptor()) // retries synchronously
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor())
  .build()
```

miguel: The fix is to make RetryInterceptor suspend-friendly (use coroutines + `call.await()`), or ensure the call creation/adapter runs on IO. Short-term workaround: set `sampleApp.useMainLooperWorkaround = true` in dev flags or add `.callbackExecutor(Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor())` to the Retrofit builder.

chandra: Does this affect API 21-23 only? Do we see it on API 30?

miguel: Only older devices where StrictMode enforces network-on-main; on API 30 it's usually fine because the Retrofit coroutine adapter falls back to a background dispatcher in many setups. On older Android the adapter can end up on main depending on how the caller is wired.

sophia: Could we move Retry to be an `EventListener` or a network interceptor? Network interceptors run on background threads, but they change semantics: they see network-level retries and not application-level `call.clone()` patterns.

kevin: Agree. NetworkInterceptor can't mutate call objects, but a Dispatcher-based retry that enqueues a new call could be a safer default for Android.

miguel: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/android-sdk/pull/412 — adds a suspend-based RetryMiddleware and updates the sample. Also updated README onboarding note: `If you hit NetworkOnMainThread, construct the SDK client with Dispatchers.IO` and include a small migration snippet.
